item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning **yes on short-run shock/inflation management**, but **not on broad social outcomes**. The 2024 record shows IMF-backed stabilization, falling inflation, reserve rebuilding, and some energy-cost correction. It also shows high debt, persistent poverty, and a still-fragile business environment.

**Positive evidence**
- **IMF Executive Board Completes Second and Final Review of the Stand-By Arrangement for Pakistan** | IMF | 2024-04-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/04/29/pr24130-pakistan-imf-executive-board-completes-second-and-final-review-sba  
  Claim: Pakistan’s policy effort had supported stabilization, with a primary surplus ahead of target, inflation declining, and reserves up from about $4.5B to about $8B. The IMF explicitly called for data-driven monetary policy and a market-determined exchange rate to absorb shocks. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7

- **Pakistan annual inflation slows to 9.6%, first single-digit stat in nearly 3 years** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-02 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/pakistan-annual-inflation-slows-to-96-first-singledigit-stat-in-nearly-3-years-3596921  
  Claim: inflation fell into single digits for the first time in nearly three years, and the finance ministry had projected roughly the same range beforehand. That supports a reading of competent inflation management rather than denial. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3

- **Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/pakistan-renegotiating-power-deals-to-cut-costs-minister-says-3606192  
  Claim: the government moved to renegotiate “unsustainable” power contracts because energy prices were hurting households and industries. That is direct evidence of response to a commodity/utility shock with cost-reduction policy. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7

- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-07-12 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff  
  Claim: the new program explicitly tied policy to disinflation, reserve buffers, flexible exchange rates, targeted subsidies through BISP, and energy tariff/cost reforms. That is strong evidence of shock management through diagnosis and correction. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.8

- **Pakistan: 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-10-10 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152  
  Claim: Pakistan had rebuilt stability, inflation had fallen significantly, the FX market was calmer, and the policy rate had been cut after disinflation. The IMF also said the government was trying to rebuild policy credibility and resilience. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7

**Negative evidence**
- **PAKISTAN: Implementing an Ambitious, Credible and Clearly Communicated Economic Reform Plan Critical for Robust Recovery, Poverty Reduction, says World Bank** | World Bank | 2024-04-02 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/01/pakistan-implementing-an-ambitious-credible-and-clearly-communicated-economic-reform-plan-critical-for-robust-recovery-p  
  Claim: growth was expected to be only 1.8% and poverty was still around 40%, with large debt, limited reserves, and import-management constraints still weighing on the economy. That is strong evidence that the crisis was not solved and gains were not yet broad-based. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.8

- **PAKISTAN: Reform Implementation Remains Critical for Continued Economic Recovery and Poverty Reduction, says World Bank** | World Bank | 2024-10-10 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank  
  Claim: growth recovered to 2.5%, but poverty rose and risks remained high because of financing needs, debt-service costs, and a loss-making power sector. That limits any claim of fully competent crisis management. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.8

- **Pakistan: 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-10-10 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152  
  Claim: the IMF still described a narrow tax base, weak governance, very low investment, insufficient health and education spending, and a difficult business environment. That is evidence that structural vulnerability and debt/inflation fragility remained unresolved. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6

- **Pakistan annual inflation slows to 9.6%, first single-digit stat in nearly 3 years** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-02 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/pakistan-annual-inflation-slows-to-96-first-singledigit-stat-in-nearly-3-years-3596921  
  Claim: Reuters noted that the IMF-backed package included higher taxes on farm incomes and electricity prices, which worried poor and middle-class households. So the stabilization was competent, but also painful and politically costly. IDs: 5B.9, 5B.8

**Search gaps**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence on **unemployment-specific management** beyond broad IMF projections and macro tables.
- I did not find a clear **sanctions-related** episode in 2024 that materially informed this lens.
- “Honesty” is mostly inferential here: the best evidence is that IMF/World Bank language and government projections tracked reality reasonably well on inflation and reserves, but I did not find an independent audit of official claims against household-level outcomes.
